messages:
From: Sophie Lim <sophie.lim@orion.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Ops Team <infra@orion.ai>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@orion.ai>

Subject: Request: regionized dedicated capacity + deal mapping (Orion.ai)

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the throughput and the fallback routing. We're heading into a firm PO for Q4 and need a pragmatic capacity plan to include in our procurement docs. High level ask: can you provide a per-region dedicated pool recommendation (US / EU / APAC) tied to our expected deal tiers and latency SLOs?

Quick context: we expect a phased rollout (APAC first, then EU, then US) driven by regulatory and latency priorities. Peak inference profile is mixed chat + embeddings; expected concurrent requests ~1400 at peak (APAC), 650 EU, 400 US with 75% chat traffic, 25% heavy embedding batch jobs. Typical seq len ~120 tokens; embeddings jobs are batched asynchronously.

We're attaching our capacity request PDF and a rough traffic projection. Ideally we'd like suggested committed SKUs, burst plan, and fallback behavior if APAC capacity is constrained. Also include a quick estimate of lead times for reserved capacity in APAC (Singapore) — procurement will need that for the PO.

Can you loop in anyone on your side for the sizing model? We want an answer by next Friday to lock internal approvals.

Thanks,
Sophie
Director, Platform Ops
Orion.ai

Attachments: orion_capacity_request_20260928.pdf (1 page summary)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lim <sophie.lim@orion.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: regionized dedicated capacity + deal mapping (Orion.ai)

Sophie — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic projection. Looping in Karthik from Capacity Planning and Marissa for commercial alignment.

High-level plan from our side:
- We will produce a 3-region committed SKU recommendation with two commitment tiers (Baseline & Growth) per region.
- For APAC (primary rollout) we’ll include a short lead-time ramp (reserve + 4-week backfill window) and a burst allowance mapped to a credit draw model.
- We'll deliver an XLSX with expected GPUs, expected 99th p95 latency impact, and estimated monthly committed cost.

To size: can you confirm the expected percent of embedding jobs that will be batched (vs ad hoc) and whether the embedding batches can tolerate 30–60s queue latency? That changes how aggressive we are on embedding-optimized SKUs.

Action items:
1) Sophie: confirm embedding batching tolerance (reply to this thread).
2) Karthik: produce preliminary SKU table and lead-time notes by Thu 01 Oct.
3) Priyom/Marissa: produce commercial mapping and recommended canary policy (APAC first) by Fri 02 Oct.

Thanks — will aim to have something you can present to procurement next week.

—Priyom
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sophie Lim <sophie.lim@orion.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: regionized dedicated capacity + deal mapping (Orion.ai)

Priyom / Sophie — preliminary SKU and lead-time notes below. This is a first-pass; I'll attach a formal XLSX in the next message.

Assumptions used:
- APAC peak concurrent = 1,400 users per your note; chat dominated (75%), average token length 120.
- Embedding batch volume: assume 60% batched with tolerance up to 45s queue time unless Sophie confirms otherwise.
- Target latency SLO (chat): 95th <= 250ms for APAC, 300ms EU, 300ms US under committed baseline.

Preliminary per-region committed guidance (Baseline / Growth):
- APAC: 32x A100-class equivalent (baseline) / 48x (growth); recommend enabling prefix KV cache + aggressive batching for chat to hit 250ms p95.
- EU: 12x A100-class equiv (baseline) / 20x (growth).
- US: 8x A100-class equiv (baseline) / 12x (growth).

Burst & fallback model:
- Include 20% burst credit pool for APAC that can be drawn for spikes; credits billed at standard burst rate.
- If committed APAC capacity exhausted, route non-SLA traffic to a lower-cost compatible model in nearby region (Tokyo <-> Singapore) with automatic fallback; for regulatory-constrained requests, we fall back to queued processing only.

Lead times (Singapore region reserved capacity):
- Typical procurement to provision reserved pool: 6–8 weeks.
- We can provision modest burst/spot-backed capacity within 2 weeks for short-term needs.

Open question for sizing accuracy: exact concurrency distribution (hourly profile) — Sophie, if you can share a 24h hour-by-hour percent, Karthik will refine the SKU numbers.

—Karthik
Senior Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lim <sophie.lim@orion.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Request: regionized dedicated capacity + deal mapping (Orion.ai)

Forwarding final packet — attached is the XLSX with per-region SKUs and a short commercial mapping. Key bullets for procurement:
- APAC Baseline: 32x A100-equivalent (estimated committed monthly cost $242k). Growth: 48x (estimated $360k).
- EU Baseline: 12x (estimated $90k). US Baseline: 8x (estimated $62k).
- Lead time Singapore reserved pool: 6–8 weeks. Spot-backed burst options available in 2 weeks.
- Canary plan: week 1 traffic routed to 25% of APAC pool; week 2 to 60%; full cutover in week 3 with automatic rollback rules on error rates/latency regressions.

Sophie — next steps from Redwood: we’ll upload the formal quote to HubSpot and share a DocuSign PO template once procurement confirms the expected baseline tier. Please confirm embedding batch tolerance (we assumed 60% with 45s). If that changes we’ll re-run the cost model.

Attachments: orion_estimated_sku_by_region.xlsx; redwood-dedicated-sku-matrix.pdf

Thanks everyone — reasonable timeline to finalize before your internal PO deadline.

—Priyom
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
